channels.what: published standards that ship an official conformance suite or test vectors
channels.hints: ISO/IEC, IETF RFC test vectors, W3C test suites, Khronos CTS, Unicode conformance files, ECMA, ITU-T reference software, IEEE 754 test suites

channels.what: language, VM, ISA and toolchain specification test suites
channels.hints: wasm spec tests, RISC-V arch tests, test262 subsets, assembler/disassembler test corpora, printf/strtod/date test corpora, linker and object-format test suites

channels.what: mid-size libraries whose own data-driven test suites (input/expected files) are runnable and portable
channels.hints: GitHub repos with tests/ of thousands of fixture files; C, Go and Java libraries; parsers, formatters, codecs, calendars, units, geometry

channels.what: libraries whose own test suites are known to build and run in a container (public environment recipes)
channels.hints: SWE-smith environment profiles: C, C++, Go, JS/TS, Python and Rust repos with a working test command

channels.what: independent permissive ports or reimplementations of a library in another language, usable as a reference
channels.hints: crates.io 'pure Rust implementation of', 'pure Go port of', 'pure Python', Zig and Swift rewrites, 'Show HN: I rewrote X in'

channels.what: real executables usable as differential oracles on generated inputs
channels.hints: assemblers, disassemblers, formula engines, typesetters, diff/patch, query dialects, font tools, image tools, CAD kernels, schedulers with exact output

channels.what: OSS-Fuzz projects with fuzz targets and seed corpora, usable as differential harnesses and input generators
channels.hints: google/oss-fuzz projects list, fuzz corpora, projects with structure-aware fuzzers

channels.what: long-standing, large-scope feature requests or RFC issues that maintainers welcomed but nobody implemented, in active permissively licensed repos (500+ stars) with big runnable test suites
channels.hints: GitHub issues labelled enhancement / feature / RFC / help wanted with many upvotes, open for a year or more, no merged or open PR implementing them; multi-part scope (several formats, modes or backends); repos in Go, Rust, TypeScript, Python, C

channels.what: real release pairs or PR series with a measured multi-x CPU speedup and unchanged output
channels.hints: CHANGELOG 'x faster', release notes, engineering blogs with benchmarks, 'performance' milestones; parsers, codecs, compressors, query engines, serializers, geometry, interpreters

channels.what: issue-tracker performance regressions or slow paths with a reproducer, a workload and a fix that touched several modules
channels.hints: GitHub issues labelled performance / regression with benchmarks, bisected slowdowns, profiling write-ups

channels.what: permissively licensed benchmark instance sets and competitions with real workloads
channels.hints: SAT/MaxSAT/SMT competitions (CC-BY records), PACE challenge, DIMACS challenges, CVRP and scheduling sets, open corpora with licences stated

channels.what: CPU-feasible train-evaluate problems with an objective metric, open data and an out-of-distribution split
channels.hints: compression and rate-distortion, heuristic search and solver configuration, classical ML with distribution shift, OCR and denoising, forecasting, program synthesis; licence must allow redistribution

channels.what: public long-horizon benchmark tasks to mutate onto a different real subject (never copy)
channels.hints: Proximal-Labs/frontier-swe, LHTB, Terminal-Bench, Commit0, GSO, SWE-Perf, RE-Bench task lists; keep the lever, change the subject

channels.what: research papers with released artifacts (code + data + evaluation scripts) whose result is a measurable engineering objective
channels.hints: artifact-evaluated papers (ACM badges), MLSys/OSDI/PLDI/SIGMOD artifacts, Papers with Code entries with CPU-scale baselines
